50926771.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human recombinant Tie2 by SPR assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a technology widely used to investigate protein–macromolecule and protein–small molecule interactions because of its advantages of label-free, sensitive, real-time, noninvasive, low sample consumption, and high throughput. In this study, it was used to evaluate the binding affinities of the leads to exTie2. The kinetic binding feature of loperamide was shown in Figure 3c. The maximal response (Rmax) value was approximately 20 response units (RU). The equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) values for loperamide, cetirizine, alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin, and Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine were 5.9 × 10−6, 9.0 × 10−5, 8.2 × 10−5, and 1.2 × 10−4 M, respectively (Fig. 3d). The tendency was consistent with that of their amber scores, that is, loperamide had the highest affinity to Tie2.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Preparation of recombinant Tie2 and SPR-based affinity determination. (a) Agarose gel electrophoresis of PCR product of Tie2 fragment and of recombinant plasmid pcDNA3.1-exTie2-His after digestion with endonucleases NotI and EcoRI. The results indicated that the Tie2 fragment was about 1400 bp. (b) SDS–PAGE and western blot profiles of purified exTie2. The recombinant exTie2 was approximately 65 kDa and was used for subsequent SPR assay. (c) SPR analysis of the binding affinity of loperamide to exTie2. (d) The equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) values of the leads. Columns A, B, C, and D represent the KD values of loperamide, cetirizine, alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin, and Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine, respectively.
original_paragraph.Figure 3c sensorgram: Figure 3c shows the SPR sensorgram for loperamide binding to exTie2. The x-axis represents time (s) from 100 to 400 s. The y-axis represents Response unit (RU) from -5 to 25. The sensorgram shows a rapid association phase followed by a dissociation phase. The maximal response (Rmax) is approximately 20 RU.
original_paragraph.Figure 3d bar chart: Figure 3d is a bar chart showing the equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) values for four compounds. The x-axis labels are A, B, C, D, representing loperamide, cetirizine, alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin, and Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine, respectively. The y-axis is KD (μM) from 0 to 140. The values are: A (loperamide) = 5.9 μM, B (cetirizine) = 90 μM, C (alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin) = 82 μM, D (Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine) = 120 μM.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. SPR-based competitive binding assay. (a) Competitive binding of loperamide. Curves 1, 2, 3, and 4 represent the binding features of angiopoietin solutions containing 0, 25, 50, and 100 μM loperamide, respectively. Loperamide interfered with the binding of both angiopoietin1 (Ang1) and angiopoietin2 (Ang2). The interference was more significant when angiopoietins were injected at higher concentrations. (b), (c) and (d) represent binding features of Ang1 solutions containing cetirizine, alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin and Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine, respectively. Curves 1, 2, and 3 represent the Ang1 solutions containing 0, 50, and 100 μM of leads, respectively.
original_paragraph.Figure 4a sensorgram: Figure 4a shows three sensorgrams for competitive binding assays. The left panel is for Ang1 (36 nM) with curves 1, 2, 3, 4 representing 0, 25, 50, 100 μM loperamide. The middle panel is for Ang2 (38 nM) with the same loperamide concentrations. The right panel is for Ang2 (76 nM) with the same loperamide concentrations. The x-axis is Time (s) from 200 to 550 s. The y-axis is Response unit (RU). The curves show that increasing loperamide concentration reduces the response, indicating competitive inhibition.
original_paragraph.Figure 4b sensorgram: Figure 4b shows the competitive binding of cetirizine to Ang1 (36 nM). Curves 1, 2, 3 represent 0, 50, 100 μM cetirizine. The x-axis is Time (s) from 200 to 550 s. The y-axis is Response unit (RU) from -50 to 350. The response is reduced with increasing cetirizine concentration.
original_paragraph.Figure 4c sensorgram: Figure 4c shows the competitive binding of alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin to Ang1 (36 nM). Curves 1, 2, 3 represent 0, 50, 100 μM alpha-aminobenzylpenicillin. The x-axis is Time (s) from 200 to 550 s. The y-axis is Response unit (RU) from -50 to 300. The response is reduced with increasing concentration.
original_paragraph.Figure 4d sensorgram: Figure 4d shows the competitive binding of Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine to Ang1 (36 nM). Curves 1, 2, 3 represent 0, 50, 100 μM Fmoc-d-2-fluorophenylalanine. The x-axis is Time (s) from 200 to 550 s. The y-axis is Response unit (RU) from -50 to 300. The response is reduced with increasing concentration.

analyte.concentration_range: 0, 25, 50, 100 μM (for competitive assays); specific concentrations for direct binding not specified
